claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloy.
The initial HEA is a homogeneous refractory alloy.
Alloy design or core-shell synthesis can produce a catalyst with a durable core and an active-species-enriched surface.
The proposed catalyst has a core-shell structure containing a refractory-element core, such as Nb, Mo, Ta, and W.
The shell is enriched with catalytically active transition metals.
The core-shell HEA will enhance HER and HOR catalytic activity relative to conventional monometallic or dilute-alloy catalysts.
The core-shell HEA will enhance durability relative to conventional monometallic or dilute-alloy catalysts.
The proposed performance applies in both acidic and alkaline HER and HOR environments.
The internal core composition provides corrosion resistance and mechanical stability.
The active shell tunes the surface electronic structure to optimize HER and HOR kinetics.
The refractory core ensures structural integrity and resistance to degradation under harsh electrochemical conditions.
Modification of the surface electronic structure by the active shell lowers HER and HOR overpotentials.
Synergistic interactions among multiple principal elements tune the adsorption energies of hydrogen intermediates.
Tuning hydrogen-intermediate adsorption energies increases catalytic activity.
The designed catalyst will exhibit lower overpotentials and higher turnover frequencies for both HER and HOR.
The designed catalyst will exhibit improved long-term operational durability.
Conventional monometallic or dilute-alloy catalysts typically have limited catalytic activity or durability under operational conditions.
Activity and durability improvements depend strongly on elemental ratios and precise control of the core-shell structure.
Changes in synthesis parameters can alter the balance between catalytic activity and durability.
The optimal elemental combination, elemental ratios, and shell thickness for simultaneously maximizing activity and durability are not yet determined.
